extraction.name: OWSM v4: Improving Open Whisper-Style Speech Models via Data Scaling and Cleaning
extraction.description: This paper introduces OWSM v4, a series of fully open speech foundation models trained on a curated dataset derived from YODAS. The work addresses challenges in large-scale web-crawled data, such as incorrect language labels and audio-text misalignments, by developing a scalable data-cleaning pipeline. The resulting dataset contains 166,000 hours of speech across 75 languages. The OWSM v4 models significantly outperform previous versions and match or surpass frontier industrial models like Whisper and MMS on multilingual benchmarks.
extraction.creator: Yifan Peng, Muhammad Shakeel, Yui Sudo, William Chen, Jinchuan Tian, Chyi-Jiunn Lin, Shinji Watanabe
extraction.citeAs: Peng, Y., Shakeel, M., Sudo, Y., Chen, W., Tian, J., Lin, C.-J., & Watanabe, S. (2025). OWSM v4: Improving Open Whisper-Style Speech Models via Data Scaling and Cleaning. Interspeech 2025.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The data was collected by integrating YODAS, a large-scale web-crawled dataset, with existing OWSM data. YODAS was originally crawled from the web. The authors developed a scalable data-cleaning pipeline to process this data.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: YODAS (Youtube-Oriented Dataset for Audio and Speech), a large-scale web-crawled dataset containing 370k hours of audio in 149 languages, and existing OWSM data.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The data cleaning pipeline consists of three steps: (1) Resegmentation: Realignment of audio and text using CTC segmentation algorithm with OWSM-CTC v3.2 model, segmenting long-form audio into 30-second utterances, and removing non-speech elements. (2) LID-based filtering: Filtering utterances where the original language label does not match predictions from text-based (fastText) and audio-based (ECAPA-TDNN) Language Identification models. (3) CTC-score-based filtering: Discarding utterances where any constituent short utterance falls within the lowest quantile of CTC confidence scores, using a threshold of theta_CTC = 0.10.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The raw YODAS data underwent a rigorous cleaning process including resegmentation, language identification filtering, and CTC-score-based filtering to remove misalignments and incorrect labels. The final cleaned dataset comprises 166k hours of audio across 75 languages. The data was then combined with existing OWSM data for training.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The raw YODAS data included text transcriptions annotated with start and end timestamps. These annotations were cleaned and realigned using automated models (OWSM-CTC, fastText, ECAPA-TDNN). No manual human annotation process is described for the final dataset.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors will publicly release the cleaned YODAS data, pre-trained models, and all associated scripts via the ESPnet toolkit. No specific versioning or deprecation policy is mentioned.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The work aims to advance open research by providing fully open speech foundation models and data, addressing concerns about privacy, transparency, and reproducibility associated with proprietary models like Whisper. The models are designed to be reproducible and accessible to academic institutions.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The distribution of languages in the cleaned YODAS data is highly imbalanced. English constitutes the largest share, while many other languages remain underrepresented. The authors kept the original distribution without resampling.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The data distribution across languages is highly imbalanced. The models were trained on academic-scale resources, which may limit performance compared to industrial-scale models in some scenarios, although they compete closely. The inference speed for AED models in ESPnet is slower due to lack of lower-level optimization compared to other frameworks.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Fine Tuning. The dataset and models are intended for multilingual automatic speech recognition (ASR), speech translation (ST), spoken language identification (LID), and voice activity detection (VAD).
